newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: YTL power unit gets nod to list in KL.
newsitem.headline: YTL power unit gets nod to list in KL.

text.p: Malaysian infrastructure developer and power concern YTL Corp Bhd has received approval from the Securities Commission to list its power generation unit on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, the national Bernama news agency said on Monday.
It quoted a YTL Corp statement as saying YTL Power International Bhd will be listed under the exchange's Infrastructure Project Companies (IPC) ruling which has more relaxed entry conditions.
Companies listed under IPC rules do not have to show a three- to five-year earnings record.
YTL Corp said the securities watchdog has also approved the restructuring of YTL Power prior to its listing, Bernama said.

Under the proposed restructuring, YTL Power will acquire 50 percent interest and one special share held by YTL Corp in YTL Power Generation Sdn Bhd (YTLPG) for 342.2 million ringgit to be paid by the issue of new YTLPG shares.
YTL Power will also acquire the balance 50 percent equity in YTLPG for 1.85 billion ringgit, by the issue of 1.85 billion convertible preference shares to the other YTLPG shareholders.

YTL Power would also acquire 51 percent equity interest in YTL-CPI Power Ltd for HK$510,000 in cash and take up a 30 percent equity in private power firm Teknologi Tenaga Perlis (Overseas) Consortium Sdn Bhd.

YTL Power will also acquire the rights, title and interest held by YTL Corp in the Hwange Power project in Zimbabwe and a proposed 500 megawatt power project in the southern Malaysian state of Johor, Bernama said.

The restructuring also includes the issue by YTL Power of 200 million convertible preference shares (CPS) for subscription by state investment agency Khazanah Nasional Bhd, 300 million CPS by YTL Corp and 62.5 million CPS by AIG Asian Infrastructure Fund.
YTL Power also plans a restricted offer for sale of up to 98.3 million shares to its shareholders.
YTL Corp said the listing of YTL Power would provide the power firm with direct access to the capital markets and facilitate the raising of funds.
